adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:17 — Header flex items keep default flex-shrink:1 and extra-info's flex-basis is its max-content width, so a long topic title shrinks .panel below its float width and the float:left icons/login buttons wrap onto extra lines (floats never shrank before); .title/.panel need flex-shrink:0 and extra-info needs min-width:0

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.header .contents` from a float-based layout to a flex container (`@include flexbox()` / `@include align-items(center)`) and removes `.title { float: left; }` and `.panel { float: right; }`, replacing the panel positioning with `margin-left: auto` and `@include order(3)`. With this switch, `.title` and `.panel` become flex items and will use the default `flex-shrink: 1`, which can allow the `.panel` content (e.g., icons/buttons) to shrink/wrap in constrained widths—behavior floats did not have. The diff does not add any `flex-shrink: 0` / `min-width` constraints to preserve the previous non-shrinking behavior, so the reported wrapping/shrinking regression is a plausible defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — margin-left:auto replaces float:right to right-align .panel, but the legacy display:-webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks the mixin emits (old Android/iOS Safari/Firefox <22) don't use auto margins to distribute free space, so the panel sits right next to the title in exactly the browsers the prefixes target

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is switched to `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` changes from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` (plus `@include order(3)`). The new `flexbox()` mixin emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks, but the diff does not add any corresponding legacy box alignment/packing rules (e.g. `-webkit-box-pack`) and relies solely on `margin-left: auto` for right-alignment. In the older box model those fallbacks target, auto margins are not a reliable way to distribute remaining space, so the panel may no longer right-align in exactly those prefixed modes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `.small-action` a flex container and explicitly sets `@include align-items(center);` (topic-post.scss around the cited line). In a row-direction flex container, `align-items: center` vertically centers children on the cross-axis. Previously, the elements flowed normally and the avatar would align to the top of the multi-line description by default. This change can therefore regress the layout by centering the avatar next to taller/multi-line content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:37 — The panel now relies only on `margin-left: auto` to stay right-aligned, but the legacy `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallbacks emitted by the new mixin treat auto margins as zero, so in those browsers the panel stops being right-aligned once `float: right` is removed.

In the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` flexbox models, auto margins don’t behave like modern flexbox (they won’t reliably consume remaining space to push an item to the end), so removing the float can cause `.panel` to no longer right-align in those fallback browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:118 — align-items mixin forwards modern values unchanged to legacy `-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align`, which expect `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so the generic abstraction emits invalid values for those inputs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that directly assigns `$alignment` to legacy properties like `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` (mixins.scss). This abstraction is not robust for inputs such as `flex-start`/`flex-end`, which those legacy syntaxes historically expect as `start`/`end`; the mixin performs no mapping. While the new usages in this diff pass `center`/`baseline` (which are fine), the mixin itself can emit incompatible values for common modern inputs, making it a concrete, diff-grounded cross-browser issue rather than a purely hypothetical style nit.
